results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 72 outlined units summarise the controlling idea of the spec paragraph aligned to them, in spec order (p01-p04, scene p05-p09, concepts p10-p14, architecture p16-p25, landing p26-p32, localization p50-p51, lifecycle p33-p37, structured data p38-p40, performance p41-p44, apps p45/p15/p46-p49, AI search p52-p55, worked p56-p60, p61, p62, p63, ca-view p64-p68, p69, conclusion p70-p71). The five callouts are apparatus and match no spec paragraph.

The outliner marked two units. Introduction ¶3 (links to neighbouring chapters plus the definition of a contact) matches p03, whose controlling idea declares both the chapter's place and the gloss of 'contact'. Listing Pages Across the Lifecycle ¶6 (IndexNow / Indexing API for jobs) matches p37, whose controlling idea is that push notification varies by engine, naming both IndexNow and the job-posting Indexing API with its expiry rule. Both pass.

Every unit serves a supporting claim: intro and concepts S1/S2, architecture S1/S4/S5, landing and localization S2/S3, lifecycle S3, structured data and performance S4, apps S5, AI search and worked example S6 with S2-S4, judging sections all, conclusion S1/S3/S4/S6. No orphan unit found.

Each table (audit, page types, rendering strategies, landing rules, lifecycle states, before/after, trade-offs, verticals) is introduced and followed by prose that draws its point (e.g. 'Three findings stand out', 'For public pages ... the decision is rarely in doubt', 'The number that went down'). Figures 1-5 carry explanatory captions tied to the claim; quotations from Google, web.dev, schema.org, Zalando, Subito, QuintoAndar, Cloudflare and Vinted are each followed by what they show, with dated or vendor evidence labelled.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary, e.g. contrast p02 ('Most marketplaces discover this late ... This chapter takes the opposite view'), cause_effect concepts ('Each of the audit's problems ... follows from how a search engine works'), contrast lifecycle ('A landing page lasts for years; a listing lasts days or weeks'), additional_support structured data ('Beyond what each URL returns, a page can also say what it is'), example p46 ('Tradeyard shows what happens without one'), contrast p54, time p60 ('is the first test'), problem_solution p71 ('not a framework but a metric'). The landing section's elaboration of the registry is carried by the forward pointer '(next section)' in the registry item and the heading; the later app subsections (forms, deep links) are joined by subheadings and by 'waits for app adoption'. No boundary misstates its relationship.

Both flow readers describe problem -> concepts -> design -> proof -> judgement, matching the declared prerequisite_order with problem_solution (scene answered by the worked example) and grouping (judging sections); neither marks any section's position unclear, and both state there is no material lost-thread point. Minor points recorded by both readers but called minor by each: the Q4 2028 / strangler sentence at the start of the worked example reads awkwardly ('The reason is the strangler, which replaces Yardstick one capability at a time: it starts at the web layer'), and '41% of them parameterized facet URLs' precedes the page-type table. Single-reader minor points: intro ¶3 density, Subito sentence placement, surrogate key, the alert-digest sentence, localization splitting the landing/listing pairing. None is a material break, so none is recorded as a failure.

The terms on does_not_know are given before or at first substantive use: SEO architecture, crawl budget, landing page, landing page generation and BFF are defined; crawl/render/index/rank, soft 404, unavailable_after with X-Robots-Tag, hreflang, IndexNow, Indexing API, scaled content and doorway abuse, product snippets vs merchant listings, Google-Extended, the rendering models (table) and LCP/INP/CLS with thresholds are explained; 'contact' and 'organic contact' are glossed in intro ¶3. noindex and lastmod are not formally defined but are self-describing and made clear by context (thin pages 'noindex, follow, so users can still use them'; 'unchanged lastmod' after the sale; lastmod used only if accurate); no reader reported them. Terms the readers flagged as unexplained (Billing by Guesswork, Common Ground, Hearthly, Motorvane, Safe Deal, Ghost Inventory, Yardstick, enforcement overlay) are on audience.already_knows or from listing-aggregate; 'facet URL' and 'strangler' are standard vocabulary for this audience (web/SEO leads, chief architects) and are explained later in the chapter.

The opening is a direct statement of the two audiences with a revenue stake, a contrast with common practice, a scoped definition, a placement paragraph and a roadmap; no dictionary opening, funnel cliché, or announcement without a claim.
The conclusion does not merely restate sections, apologise, or open new topics; it synthesises the design, answers Ingrid's question and hands off to data-platform through the metric.

From Pages to Data ¶1 synthesises the architecture (server-rendered pages owned by clear teams, URLs from identifiers, lifecycle rules from the event stream) and states the consequence (rendering change becomes a page team's decision within a group standard, the bikes split runs as a pipeline); ¶2 names the decisive change as a metric, organic contacts instead of indexed URLs, and why its definition matters.

'That is the answer to Ingrid's question' and 'Femke's bike would have answered noindex from the minute it left search instead of collecting 37 clicks over nine days' call back to the scene's question and the sold bike; 'two most demanding clients: people on phones and the crawlers' calls back to intro ¶1.

The intro reader predicted all fifteen sections in the spec's order (scene with the 40M URLs and Femke's bike, concepts, stack, landing pages with localization, lifecycle, structured data, performance, apps, AI engines, worked example, trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, CA view, questions) and the evidence kinds (Google and web.dev documentation, schema.org, dated marketplace posts, fictional Veldmark), plus the thesis (landing pages as asset, lifecycle-driven URLs, server rendering, page ownership, BFFs). Its uncertainties (rendering and composition inside the stack section) do not contradict the roadmap.

The AC-1 reader gave every expected element: a landing set from measured demand and live supply with a minimum-results rule over weeks and an attribute-depth limit, other search URLs noindex/404 and out of sitemaps; gone listings noindex during a grace period then 410, 200 with similar listings and unavailable_after for the few still ranking; canonical URLs, sitemaps and gone status driven by ListingSold and the four SEO services; rejection of the client-rendered rebuild in favour of server rendering with one owning team per URL pattern and a web and mobile BFF; and success judged by organic contacts per thousand organic sessions, not indexed URLs.
